_meta.why: The detail index opens every day on whatever document arrives first -- an access line, an exception log or a grant log -- so each daily index's field types are decided by chance. This pins the fields whose type matters to a query (ranges on http_status/response_size, date ranges on _time, booleans for the two flags) and leaves every other string to dynamic mapping.
_meta.measured_from: 2026-09-16 readout of polaris-logs-* (run 1789463971, 508 docs): http_status, response_size, sequence, threadId (removed 2026-09-16), exception.refId arrive as JSON integers; _time as an RFC3339 string with nanoseconds; access_log_parse_error / secret_redacted as booleans (absent on a normal record).
_meta.strings_left_dynamic: superseded by v6_2026-09-16: undeclared strings follow dynamic_templates.strings_keyword_only.
_meta._time: date with the nanos format: Polaris writes 9 fractional digits. ignore_malformed so a surprise value costs the field, never the document.
_meta.removed_2026-09-16: threadId mapping dropped: threadName, threadId and ndc are removed by polaris_field_trim (fluent-bit/values.yaml FILTER 4). Indices created before the upgrade still hold them.
_meta.not_retroactive: applies only to indices created after it is applied.
_meta.v6_2026-09-16: REVIEW-pipeline P8 (decided: Kade). Strings were dynamic text + .keyword, i.e. analysed AND keyword-indexed. Now: every undeclared string is text with index:false (kept in _source, not analysed) plus the same .keyword sub-field every query in the repo already uses, so field paths do not change across old and new daily indices. message (the raw Polaris line; was _msg until schema v6) and exception.message stay full-text, without a keyword copy. client_ip is ip. CAVEAT: exists/term/match on a bare undeclared string (e.g. loggerName) finds nothing in new indices -- use loggerName.keyword.
